chunks: Al-Naḍr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:
Regarding merchants who came to a land and agreed among themselves not to sell their merchandise except at whatever price they wished, he said: “There is no harm in that.”

key_terms.اشْتَرَكُوا: they jointly agreed or entered into a shared arrangement
key_terms.بَيْعَهُمْ: their sale or merchandise being sold
key_terms.تُجَّارٍ: merchants or traders engaged in commerce
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for merchants to agree among themselves on the price at which they will sell goods?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning merchants who mutually agree on the price at which they will sell their goods. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام states that there is no harm in such an arrangement, indicating its permissibility in this context.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3958 - Al-Nadr narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan that Abu Abdullah (as), said
regarding merchants who arrived at a land and agreed among themselves not to sell their goods except at a price they desired: "There is no harm in that."
